This first bail application has been filed by the applicant under Section 438 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.06/2024, registered at Police Station Mahila Thana, District Shivpuri (M.P.) for offences punishable under Sections 376 and 506 of the IPC.

sentences.text: A s per the case of prosecution, prosecutrix claiming to be aged around 24 years and submitted a written complaint with Police Station Women Cell, Shivpuri on 23.02.2024 inter alia stating that Sonu Sharma (present applicant) is a friend of her husband.
Sonu used to visit her home.
On 15.02.2024, around 7:00 in the evening, she was alone at home.
Sonu came to her home and Sunil@Sonu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4622366/

sentences.text: 1 informed that her husband has met with an accident, therefore, she went with Sonu in his four wheeler vehicle.
Sonu stopped the car at a secluded place near Shivpuri and committed rape on her.
Sonu threatened to kill her, if she informs anybody.
Sonu left her near four lane in Subhashpura.
She returned home next morning.
After 3-4 days, her husband returned from work.
She informed her husband about the incident, but due to fear of social disrepute, they did not report.
On advice of her husband, she had come to report.
On such allegations, Police Station Women Cell registered FIR at Crime No.06/2024 for offence punishable under Sections 376 and 506 of IPC.
Prosecutrix was forwarded for medico legal examination.
No definite opinion about recent sexual intercourse was given by the Medical Officer.
Statements of prosecutrix were recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of CrPC.
Investigation is underway.

Learned counsel in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant has falsely been implicated in the matter due to dispute of applicant with the husband of prosecutrix over outstanding payment of money.
The delay in lodging the FIR without plausible reason substantiate chances of false implication.
Learned counsel referring to copy of Aadhar Card of prosecutrix, submits that her date of birth is shown as 01.01.1981, she has wrongfully mentioned age 24 years in the complaint.
Learned counsel further submits that applicant is aged around 30 years and is Driver by profession.
He is sole bread earner of the family.
He has responsibility of his old paralytic mother, therefore, there is no likelihood of absconsion leaving his family, home and profession.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
There is no likelihood of tampering with evidence as both the parties relate to same socio- economic status.
No custodial interrogation is required in the matter.
Applicant is ready to co-operate with the investigation.
Jail incarceration on false allegations would cause social disrepute to the family of the applicant.
Therefore, applicant may be extended benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned counsel for the State ably assisted by learned counsel for the objector opposes the application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Learned counsel submits that applicant has never been available for investigation.
Therefore, applicant may not be extended benefit of anticipatory bail.

On request of the Court, learned counsel for the State goes to the case diary and submits that FSL report merely shows traces of semen on undergarment of victim, but no semen was found on sanitary pad or vaginal slide of the applicant.
The call detail report gathered during investigation shows presence of applicant at the time of alleged incident at a distant place.
Further, one live-in relationship documents was also available in the case diary, which shows prosecutrix is living in relationship with her husband and her age is shown to be 30 years.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Thus, the application is allowed.
